title: U.S. House · Georgia's 6th Congressional District
area: Western suburbs of Atlanta, including parts of Cobb and Fulton counties.

context.text: Incumbent Lucy McBath (D) previously represented the old 6th District (2019-2023) and the old 7th District (2023-2025) before running in and winning this redrawn 6th District seat in 2024; she advanced unopposed from the Democratic primary. Kevin Martin won the Republican primary over Justin Pinker.

candidates.name: Lucy McBath
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Georgia's 6th Congressional District (since 2025; previously represented Georgia's 7th District 2023-2025 and Georgia's 6th District 2019-2023)

summary.text: Lucy McBath is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 6th Congressional District. She previously represented the district's earlier boundaries from 2019 to 2023 and Georgia's 7th District from 2023 to 2025, running in the redrawn 6th District in 2024. Before Congress she was a flight attendant and a gun-safety advocate with Everytown for Gun Safety and Moms Demand Action following the 2012 killing of her son.

background.text: Born in Joliet, Illinois, in 1960; earned a bachelor's degree in political science and English from Virginia State University in 1982.
Worked as a flight attendant and later as a professional advocate for Everytown for Gun Safety and Moms Demand Action, and as an author.

priorities.text: Says she is fighting to expand access to affordable health care, protect those with pre-existing conditions, and lower the cost of prescription drugs.
With the New Democrat Coalition, released an Affordability Agenda to lower costs in health care, housing, energy, family care, and household essentials.

positions.summary: Serves as Vice Chair of the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force and says she was instrumental in passing the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act.
positions.quote: Since coming to Congress, McBath has been instrumental in passing the Bipartisan Safer Communities Law.

positions.summary: Her Affordability Agenda calls for expanding access to care by fully funding Medicaid and strengthening Medicare's guaranteed benefits.
positions.quote: Expand access to care by fully funding Medicaid and strengthening Medicare’s guaranteed benefits.

positions.summary: Her official site says she believes the country must address climate change while securing a sustainable energy future, and supports increased investment in sustainable energy.
positions.quote: Congresswoman McBath believes we must address climate change while securing a sustainable energy future. She supports increased investment in sustainable energy and increasing incentives for homeowners who utilize solar or other forms of renewable energy.

positions.summary: Her Affordability Agenda calls for increasing the minimum wage.
positions.quote: Increase the minimum wage and ensure workers have a seat at the table.

positions.summary: Her Affordability Agenda calls for rolling back the Trump administration's tariffs.
positions.quote: Restore certainty by rolling back Trump’s tariffs and advancing smarter, durable trade policies.

positions.summary: Her Affordability Agenda calls for cutting red tape and updating permitting and zoning to build more homes.
positions.quote: Cut red tape and update permitting and zoning to build four million homes in the next decade.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on the Judiciary (Crime and Federal Government Surveillance Subcommittee) and the Committee on Education and the Workforce in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Released the Affordability Agenda with the New Democrat Coalition, a policy roadmap on health care, housing, energy, family care, and household costs.

candidates.name: Kevin Martin
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary over Justin Pinker.

summary.text: Kevin Martin is an accounting and finance controller and the Republican nominee for Georgia's 6th Congressional District, campaigning on youth education programs, elder care costs, and controlled growth in the district.

background.text: Graduated from Campbell High School; earned bachelor's degrees from the Georgia Institute of Technology in 1989 and Georgia State University in 1998; has worked in accounting and finance for over 35 years, including 25 years as a controller.

priorities.text: Says he will focus on education and youth development programs to attract young families to the district.
Says he wants to address elderly medical costs and reduce what he calls unnecessary tests and drug prescriptions.

positions.summary: Says insurers and doctors are taking advantage of the elderly through unnecessary tests and prescriptions, and wants to eliminate that waste, without stating a broader coverage position.
